title: Sample pack: Imaginary Botany of Planet Orrin

scenarios.text: A greenhouse keeper on Orrin notices that a tray of ember moss has stopped glowing warm at night, and the tray sits next to a cold vent. The figure shows one moss cushion with its heat bulb labelled A.

figure.caption: Ember moss cushion; A marks the heat bulb.

questions.stem: Which part of a glowroot stores the light it gathers during the day?

options.explanation: The sample notes call the lumen sac the glowroot's light store.
The root crown anchors the plant; it stores nothing.
Drift hairs take in water vapour, not light.
The bark ring is protective only.

questions.summary: Glowroots store daylight in the lumen sac.

questions.stem: A glowroot's drift hairs are trimmed off. What happens first?

options.explanation: Trimming the drift hairs doesn't change the light store.

options.text: It takes in less water vapour
options.explanation: Drift hairs are where water vapour comes in, so less is taken in.
The root crown is a separate structure.
The notes don't link the hairs to the bark ring.

questions.summary: Drift hairs take in water vapour.

sources.locator: part 1, "the drift hairs pull in vapour"

questions.stem: Which structure keeps a glowroot fixed in loose soil?

options.explanation: The lumen sac stores light.
Drift hairs take in water vapour.
The root crown is the anchoring structure.
The root crown does this.

questions.summary: The root crown anchors the glowroot.

questions.stem: A glowroot has a torn lumen sac but every other part is intact. What would a keeper see that evening?

options.explanation: With nowhere to store light, there's nothing to glow with.
The lumen sac is the light store, so a torn sac leaves little to release.
Anchoring is the root crown's job, and it is intact.
The drift hairs, which take in vapour, are intact.

questions.summary: No light store means little or no glow.

questions.stem: Orrin's night lasts twice as long as usual. How does a glowroot's evening glow change?

options.explanation: The glow starts at dusk, whatever the night's length.
The same store spread over longer gives a dimmer glow.
The store still empties, just more slowly.

options.text: It is dimmer but lasts longer
options.explanation: The notes say the stored light is rationed across the night.

questions.summary: Stored light is rationed across the night.

questions.stem: How does one skyvine warn its neighbours about frost?

options.explanation: The sample notes describe a sweet scent as the frost warning.
Colour change is a growth sign, not a warning.
Tendrils drop only in drought.
Skyvines make no sound in the notes.

questions.stem: A skyvine is grown alone in a sealed jar and frost arrives. What does it still do?

options.explanation: It still responds to frost itself.
Releasing the scent doesn't depend on neighbours being there.
Growth direction isn't linked to frost.
Not described anywhere in the notes.

questions.summary: The scent is released whether or not neighbours are present.

sources.locator: part 1, "released whether or not neighbours are near"

questions.stem: Which of these speed up skyvine growth?

options.explanation: True, but not the only one.
True, but not the only one.
True, but not the only one.
The notes list all three as growth boosters.

questions.summary: Warm wind, double-moon nights and mineral fog all speed growth.

questions.stem: Choose the INCORRECT statement about skyvine growth.

options.explanation: Correct statement: warm wind speeds growth, so still air slows it.
Correct statement, from the growth-booster list.

options.text: Skyvines grow fastest in total darkness
options.explanation: Incorrect statement: the notes say double-moon nights speed growth, so the vines need some light.
Correct statement, from the drought slide.

questions.summary: Skyvines need some light to grow fast.

questions.stem: Which structure in the figure has most likely cooled down?

options.explanation: The fronds carry heat; they don't make it.
The heat bulb makes the warmth, so cold air on it stops the warm glow.
The tray isn't part of the moss.
The vent is the cause, not a moss structure.

questions.summary: The heat bulb makes ember moss warm.

questions.stem: What should the keeper do first?

options.text: Move the tray away from the vent
options.explanation: Removing the cold source comes first in the care steps.
Water doesn't fix a cold heat bulb.
That would stop the glow for good.
Mineral fog helps skyvines, not ember moss.

questions.stem: After the tray is moved, how long until the warm glow returns, according to the notes?

options.explanation: The bulb has to rewarm first.
Far too long; the notes give one night.
The notes say the bulb rewarms within a day.
The damage can be undone.

questions.summary: The glow returns by the next night.

questions.stem: What colour is the ember moss glow at its hottest?

options.explanation: Red is the cooler glow on the slide.
Orange is the middle of the range.
Green is the glowroot's colour, not the moss's.
The slide says white; the notes say pale yellow.

preflag.note: The sample slide says white, but the sample notes say pale yellow.
